solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Airy-fairy Mrs May, trapped by emotional extremes, gets rid of Boris finally

indicators.note: something trapped is held inside, so one piece sits within the other
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

indicators.note: to get rid of something is to throw it away, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: Theresa May, British prime minister 2016-19

indicators.note: finally points at what comes at the very end, so only the closing letter is wanted

parts.note: the last letter of the name

explanation.surface: A dismissive jibe that Theresa May is woolly and emotional, and has sacked Boris Johnson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mrs May' is Theresa May, British prime minister when this appeared; Boris Johnson resigned as her Foreign Secretary in 2018, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something light, delicate and insubstantial, too refined or vague to be of this world; the words are near synonyms.

clue.text: Dished dirt about hot bit

indicators.note: a dish is ruined or spoilt, so the letters are wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone spread gossip about a racy, steamy passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dished dirt' reads as a set phrase meaning gossiped, but 'Dished' is the signal to rearrange 'dirt' together with H.
explanation.definitionFit: A third is one portion of something divided into three equal parts, so it is a share or piece of the whole.

clue.text: Attlee up for resurrection with English military-style decoration

indicators.note: something resurrected is raised in a new form, so the letters come back in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: The post-war Labour prime minister Clement Attlee is being dug up for revival, in a mock-military English fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up for' looks like 'being considered for', but 'up' is fodder; 'for resurrection' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An epaulette is the ornamental shoulder piece on a uniform jacket, originally on soldiers' and officers' coats.

clue.text: Tabloid lover no longer smooth

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to press clothes is to iron them smooth

explanation.surface: A tabloid newspaper's former sweetheart has lost their charm.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Express is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Express is one of Britain's popular mass-circulation daily newspapers in compact format, the kind called a tabloid.

clue.text: Penis hoisted by, er, booty-seeker

indicators.note: in a down answer, hoisting lifts the letters so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: tool is slang for the male member
taken as written

explanation.surface: A smutty, hesitant line about someone chasing a different kind of booty.
explanation.walkthrough: The hesitant 'er' looks like filler but supplies the last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A looter goes after plunder, and booty is goods seized or stolen, so a looter is one seeking it.

clue.text: Bill to Hillary: "suppose president's first to go mad"

indicators.note: something mad is disordered, so the remaining letters are jumbled
first picks out the opening letter, the one that will be taken away
something told to go leaves, so a letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
the first letter of the word, the one removed

explanation.surface: Bill Clinton muses to Hillary about a president going off his head.
explanation.walkthrough: SUPPOSE drops one P, and the remaining six letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Clinton is Hillary Clinton's husband, so to her he is the marriage partner; the definition works by example.

clue.text: Do a warm-up exercise: after second time, vomit

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
T is the abbreviation for time
to retch is to heave as if to be sick

explanation.surface: An over-ambitious gym session: after a second go at the warm-up, someone throws up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second time' looks like a phrase meaning 'again', but each word gives a single abbreviated letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretching the muscles is the usual loosening routine done before sport, so it is the verb for that preparatory activity.

clue.text: Broadcasting negative raised by Sky

indicators.note: in a down answer, raising lifts the letters so they read upwards

parts.note: no is a negative reply
the sky is the air above us

explanation.surface: A gripe about Sky, the British satellite TV company, putting out negative programming.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky reads as the broadcaster Sky TV, which fits the surface, but it simply means the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme that is being transmitted live is said to be on air, the radio and television idiom for transmitting.

clue.text: Weinstein, not popular, amazingly takes Private Eye for a drink

indicators.note: something amazing is extraordinary and out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged
not marks something to leave out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Harvey Weinstein, the disgraced film producer
in means fashionable or popular; these letters are taken out
the magazine speaks of itself in the editorial plural

explanation.surface: The unpopular Weinstein surprisingly takes the magazine out for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: WEINSTEIN loses IN to give WESTEIN; adding WE, the editorial voice of Private Eye, gives the nine letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet wine, such as a dessert wine, is an alcoholic beverage, so it is one kind of drink; definition by example.

clue.text: (& 15dn.) Elected, fit — response to stimulus is e.g. unwelcome "pussy-grabbing"

parts.note: a candidate who is elected gets in
fit in the sense of suitable
how an organism responds to stimuli

explanation.surface: A dig at Donald Trump, elected despite his boast about grabbing women, behaviour widely condemned.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across two lights, 9 across and 15 down. 'Pussy-grabbing' refers to Trump's notorious recorded boast.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwanted groping is the standard example of conduct that is improper, the phrase used in harassment complaints; definition by example.

clue.text: Wedding vow needs latitude, darling

parts.note: the words said in the marriage ceremony
L is the abbreviation for latitude

explanation.surface: Someone tells their darling that their wedding vows need some leeway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latitude' suggests freedom, which fits the surface, but it is only the abbreviation L, as on maps.
explanation.definitionFit: A darling, in the sense of a favourite adored by all, such as the darling of the crowd, is an adored hero.

clue.text: Who's responsible for Brexit? Elite circle (tear spilled)

parts.note: the elect are a chosen elite

indicators.note: something spilled is scattered and messed up, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: O is round like a circle
taken as written

explanation.surface: Who is to blame for Brexit? The metropolitan elite, says one side, with a tear shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elite circle' reads as one phrase, but splits into two pieces; 'tear' is the bit to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The 2016 referendum result was decided by the voters, so the whole voting population is who brought Brexit about.

clue.text: Retreat with tits out, as one who might be on the pull

definitions.text: one who might be on the pull

parts.note: a den is a private retreat

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or not in place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bawdy picture of someone topless in their hideaway, out to pick somebody up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the pull' is British slang for looking for a sexual partner; here it means pulling teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Extracting teeth is part of the job of this medical professional, so the pull is a tooth extraction, not a seduction.

clue.text: Sex? Tripe, gruesome — requires energy, ability!

indicators.note: something gruesome is horribly mangled, so the letters are twisted out of shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A complaint that bad sex takes stamina and skill.
explanation.walkthrough: E for energy joins the fodder before the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Expertise is specialist skill or know-how, so it is a near synonym for competence or capability.

clue.text: Bill Cash snapped "Get rid of Labour leader", which is very dry

definitions.note: a description of the answer rather than a noun for it

indicators.note: something snapped is broken, so the letters are broken up and reassembled
getting rid of something discards it, so a letter is removed
a leader comes at the front, so the opening letter is meant

parts.note: Bill Cash, the veteran Eurosceptic Conservative MP
the first letter of the word, which is removed

explanation.surface: The Tory Bill Cash barks a demand to oust Jeremy Corbyn, a remark as dry as they come.
explanation.walkthrough: BILLCASH loses one L, and the remaining seven letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Chablis is a white Burgundy known for its crisp, bone-dry character, so it is a famously dry wine.

clue.text: see 9ac.
Ed's half into pisspoor Spears covers

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it
something piss-poor is badly done, so the letters are botched into a new order

parts.note: Britney Spears, the pop singer

indicators.note: half of a two-letter word is just one of its letters, here the back one

parts.note: the second half of ED

explanation.surface: Ed Sheeran's contribution to some dreadful Britney Spears cover versions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers' looks like a noun for cover versions, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread something over a surface is to coat it, so the verb is a synonym in the third person singular.

clue.text: Two-faced quality of the French and Italy, sadly

parts.note: du is French for 'of the'

indicators.note: something gone sadly awry is spoiled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A jibe at the French and Italians in Brexit talks as two-faced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two-faced' suggests deceit, but here it means simply having two sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Duality is the state of having two parts or aspects, so two faces make a double nature.

clue.text: He is in banking; he is pissing around in Rolls Royce?

definitions.note: a clause describing the answer rather than a noun

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

parts.note: a Rolls Royce is a luxury car, an example, hence the question mark

indicators.note: pissing around means messing about, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: the two short words taken as written

explanation.surface: A sneer at bankers: one fooling about in his Rolls Royce.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged pair of words sits inside CAR; the question mark flags the Rolls Royce as just one example of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A cashier works behind the counter of a bank handling money, so the job is literally being in banking.

clue.text: Keeping pace with a tit

parts.note: taken as written
tit is slang for a breast

explanation.surface: Someone running alongside a small garden bird, or a crude joke about a busty companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tit' could be the bird, as in keeping pace with a small bird, but it is the slang sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping abreast means staying level and up to date, side by side, the idiom for not falling behind.

clue.text: (& 23ac.) Underwear row — Sun skewers old soldier

parts.note: a row or line of things threaded together has a six-letter name, as with beads or pearls

indicators.note: a skewer is driven through the middle, so one piece ends up inside another

parts.note: a vet is a veteran
S is the abbreviation for Sun, as for Sunday

explanation.surface: The Sun tabloid lays into an old soldier over a row about underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across two lights, 20 down and 23 across. 'Row' looks like a quarrel, but it means a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A string vest is a mesh undershirt, a famously unglamorous British garment, so it is an item worn under clothes.

clue.text: Ex-PM: question intelligence

parts.note: Earl Grey, prime minister 1830-34
a matter is a question or issue to be dealt with

explanation.surface: A former prime minister has his brainpower questioned.
explanation.walkthrough: Earl Grey, after whom the tea is named, was the Whig prime minister behind the 1832 Reform Act.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey matter is brain tissue, used informally to mean brains or brainpower.

clue.text: Maxwell's property he went off ultimately?

definitions.text: Maxwell's property he went off ultimately?

parts.note: surface reading: a possession of the late media tycoon Robert Maxwell
setter's reading: the thing he finally went over the side of, since Maxwell drowned after vanishing from his boat in 1991

explanation.walkthrough: 'Went off' sounds like left or went bad, but it means literally fell off; the question mark admits the riddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Maxwell owned the luxury vessel Lady Ghislaine and was found dead in the sea after going overboard from it.

clue.text: see 20dn.
Issue surrounding Trump's and May's ends — keep under observation

parts.note: issue means offspring, so a son

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so the last letters are kept

parts.note: the final letter of the name
the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: A row over Trump's and May's political endings, with the surveillance state watching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a matter for debate, but it means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: To spy on someone is to watch them secretly, so the phrasal verb means to monitor.

clue.text: Screwed in minicar by politician, making you look bad

parts.note: taken as written
a Tory is a Conservative politician

explanation.walkthrough: 'Screwed' looks like part of the scandal, but it signals the rearrangement of the next two words.

clue.text: Upper classes want short military officer put on trial

parts.note: GEN is the short form of general
a try is an attempt or trial

explanation.surface: The posh set want a diminutive army officer court-martialled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like a description of a small officer, but it shortens the rank.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the landed families just below the nobility, so they form the upper ranks of society.

clue.text: "Go on the piss," grunted rum King

indicators.note: rum means odd or peculiar, so the letters are put into a strange new order

parts.note: taken as written
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: An odd monarch grunts an order to go out on a bender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink, which suits the boozy surface, but it is the signal meaning strange. 'On the piss' is British slang for a drinking session.
explanation.definitionFit: Going on the piss is British slang for a heavy session of boozing, so it means to become intoxicated.
